analysis.title: Fab Five: five reasons this new bull will have much more room to run
key_insights: The S&P 500 semiconductor index trades at 13.8x forward earnings, a 25% discount to the broader market and the widest relative discount since December 2018, per Scott Rubner.
The SOX forward P/E discount to the S&P 500 is near its widest in 15 years, per Peter Callahan.
The Nasdaq 100 forward P/E has fallen to around 19x, approaching levels last seen in the 2022 bear market, though the index is not currently in a bear market (Citadel).
Microsoft printed a fresh all-time high and Apple rose more than 5% on Wednesday, its best session in 18 months. Two of the world's three largest companies are at new highs.
Brent fell roughly $18 in five sessions, one of its sharpest five-day declines in recent history (GS trading desk). US wholesale gasoline prices hit a seven-month low.

US buyback authorizations reached a record $1.3 trillion this year, more than 10% above 2025 levels. Per Goldman's trading desk, companies in open repurchase windows are set to rise from roughly 300 to nearly 500 in the coming days.

Since 1952, the 12 months after a midterm election have been the strongest stretch of the four-year cycle for the S&P 500. Across 18 midterms, the index averaged +7.5% through year end, +13.9% over 6 months and +15.5% over 12 months, and was higher at both the 6 and 12 month points in all 18 instances (GS Market Data).
Year three of the presidential cycle has historically been the strongest, with average S&P 500 gains of 14%, and next year is year three (Sean Emory).

sector_views.rationale: Forward P/E of 13.8x is a 25% discount to the S&P 500, the widest relative discount since December 2018.
Nasdaq 100 forward P/E near 19x, close to 2022 bear-market levels, while mega-cap leaders are making new highs.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A sharp oil decline is feeding through to gasoline and could support consumer spending into the holiday season if sustained.
Lower fuel costs could help consumers heading into the holiday season.

risk_factors: The piece opens by acknowledging that bears have had plenty to talk about lately, but it names no specific bear-side risks.
vol_and_positioning: Corporate buyback windows are set to expand from roughly 300 to nearly 500 companies in the coming days, adding to the corporate bid into year-end (GS trading desk).
US buyback authorizations are at a record $1.3 trillion this year.
